name: Skater
stable: Trunk, pelvis and the standing leg
summary: Low squat stance, one foot on the platform and one on the carriage. One leg holds the squat while the other presses the carriage out to the side.
steps: Stand side-on, one foot on the platform and one on the carriage edge.
Sit into a small squat, chest tipped forward, hands behind the back.
Shift most of the weight onto the platform leg.
Breathe out to press the carriage leg straight; breathe in to bend it back with control.

layers.title: Weight on the platform leg
layers.text: The carriage leg does the pressing.

layers.title: Weight on the carriage leg
layers.text: Hold the squat on the carriage side and let the platform leg straighten — harder to control.

layers.title: Weight shift
layers.text: Press out, glide the weight across to the other leg, then draw the carriage in; add running arms.

layers.title: Holds and tempo
layers.text: Hold at the widest point or slow the return.

cautions.note: Wide stance on a moving carriage.

cues:
Stay low — the head doesn't bob up as the leg straightens.
Ribs stay closed and the spine long.
Standing knee tracks over the middle toes.
Slow on the way in.

review.note: Draft entry written for OpenPilates. Needs review by a qualified Pilates instructor before teaching from it.

variations.name: Carriage foot closer to the middle of the carriage for less resistance
